title: Are Indians Accustomed to Trade Time for Free? A Neuro-Economic Exploration
abstract: This chapter presents a neuro-economic exploration of how individuals evaluate and trade time and monetary resources during decision-making. It examines the psychological and neurocognitive processes underlying time–money choices, highlighting how the subjective valuation of resources can shape economic decisions. The chapter situates these processes within the Indian context and discusses their relevance for understanding resource allocation and decision behaviour.

title: Cortical Desynchronization and Autonomic Reactivity under Acute Cognitive Stress
abstract: Investigated the temporal coupling between EEG frequency shifts (alpha/beta ratio) and electrodermal responses (GSR) during cognitive workload and decision-making tasks, highlighting coupled central and autonomic mobilization.

title: Heart Rate Variability (HRV) as a Predictor of Emotional Regulation Capacity in Virtual Reality
abstract: Evaluated high-frequency HRV (HF-HRV) in immersive virtual environments designed to elicit relaxation and stress recovery, verifying the utility of autonomic indicators in emotion regulation.
